biodiversity_overview.text: 3,557 GBIF occurrence records for 41 tracked species are attributed to Jammu & Kashmir, spanning 1886-2026.
3,490 of these records (98.1%) are located to within 10 km.

species_richness.text: Observed tracked species by group: Aves 18, Magnoliopsida 9, Mammalia 8, Squamata 2, Pinopsida 1, Amphibia 1, Testudines 1, Cephalopoda 1.

threatened_species.text: 3 species with records here are officially threatened (IUCN CR/EN/VU). Names and categories from the IUCN Red List export are not shown in this public snapshot.
1 further species are threatened according to the project's unverified reference list: Sloth Bear (VU).

notable_species.text: Most recorded species: Indian Paradise-flycatcher (498), Indian White-eye (398), Indian Grey-Hornbill (362), Indian Golden Oriole (308), Indian Pond-heron (285).

temporal_trends.text: Records per year went from 59 in 2016 to 29 in 2025. This reflects recording effort as much as wildlife and is not a population trend.

protection_coverage.text: Wildlife protected areas (OpenStreetMap national parks, sanctuaries and reserves) cover 4.35% of Jammu & Kashmir's area (18 areas intersect the state).
7.1% of precisely located records fall inside these areas (248 of 3,490); this is not a measure of habitat protection.

risk_indicators.text: Highest model-predicted vulnerability among species recorded here (MODEL PREDICTION, not IUCN status): Jacquemont's Hazel (0.62), Small Indian Mongoose (0.47), Indian Gooseberry (0.35), Common Cat Snake (0.35), Sloth Bear (0.29).

conservation_priority.text: Top experimental CIPI grid cells in Jammu & Kashmir (equal-weight reference): cell near 34.125N 74.625E (overall rank 245, median rank across weightings 271); cell near 32.625N 74.625E (overall rank 286, median rank across weightings 288); cell near 32.625N 75.375E (overall rank 340, median rank across weightings 328).

environmental_pressures.text: Tree cover of at least 30% canopy covered 13,351 km2 (23.78% of land) in 2000 (Hansen Global Forest Change; includes plantations).

47.2 km2 of that tree cover was lost in 2001-2024 (0.35% of the 2000 extent; 0.04% in 2015-2024, rank 29 of 35 states). The largest annual loss was in 2004 (9.66 km2). Loss includes plantation harvest and natural disturbance; regrowth is not subtracted.
Built-up surfaces cover 1.23% of land and population density is 335.1 people per km2 (GHSL 2020).
39% of 30 m tree-cover pixels lie on a forest edge (a fragmentation indicator; higher means more fragmented).
These describe pressures on places; they do not show effects on any species.
